Examples

Box3D offline: tower knockdown

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Run itPut it on itch.ioHow it worksGoing further

A single-player Box3D example with no Kit, no Replay and no network: one script owns a Box3D world and steps it itself. Start here if you want Box3D physics in an offline game.

A pyramid of 15 boxes stands on the ground. The HUD counts the boxes knocked down.

Control Action
Left click or Space Launch a ball from the camera toward the mouse
Hold right mouse button and drag Orbit the camera around the middle of the stack
W / S (or Up / Down) Move the camera in and out
R Rebuild the tower

Run it#

From the repository root:

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/box3d_offline/play.sh

play.sh builds the Box3D native library into the ignored .box3d-cache (about 15 seconds the first time), builds the scripts, and opens the game. To use a native library you already built, set BOX3D_NATIVE_LIBRARY to its libogb3.dylib or libogb3.so. The build copies that library into bin/ next to the SDK core, which loads it at startup.

To work on it in the Godot editor, pass -e; other arguments go to Godot as well:

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/box3d_offline/play.sh -e

The editor rebuilds the scripts whenever you save an .odin file, and that rebuild needs BOX3D_NATIVE_LIBRARY, which play.sh sets for you. If you open the project another way, such as from Godot's Project Manager, it still runs, but saving a script fails to link Box3D and keeps the previous build until you run play.sh again.

Put it on itch.io#

Build the browser version and the zip itch.io expects:

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/box3d_offline/export_web.sh

This writes out/web/ and out/box3d-offline-web.zip (about 12 MB, index.html at its root). It builds Box3D for WebAssembly, links it into the game's single wasm module, and runs Godot's Web export with the preset in export_presets.cfg. Try it locally before uploading; serve.sh adds the headers the browser build needs:

Shell
nix develop --command bash build/serve.sh examples/box3d_offline/out/web

Then open http://localhost:8099/. On itch.io:

  1. Create a new project and set Kind of project to HTML.
  2. Upload out/box3d-offline-web.zip and tick This file will be played in the browser.
  3. Under Embed options, set the viewport to 1280 × 720 (or enable the fullscreen button), and tick SharedArrayBuffer support. The build uses threads, which need it; without it the page stays blank.
  4. Save and view the page.

For repeated uploads, itch's butler command-line tool can push the zip: butler push examples/box3d_offline/out/box3d-offline-web.zip USER/GAME:html5.

How it works#

Everything is in scripts/tower.odin:

  • Building the world. build_world calls world_create, then body_create and shape_box for the static ground and each dynamic box. A reset destroys the world, which destroys every body in it, and builds a fresh one.
  • Stepping. box_tower_physics_process calls world_step_fixed once per Godot physics frame. That call always advances 1/60 s, so project.godot keeps the physics rate at 60 Hz.
  • Launching. launch_ball turns the mouse position into a camera ray and creates a dynamic sphere with that starting velocity. is_bullet turns on continuous collision so a fast ball cannot pass through a box. Up to eight balls exist at once; the ninth recycles the oldest.
  • Camera. box_tower_process runs every rendered frame, separately from the physics. While the right button is held it turns mouse movement into yaw and pitch around the stack, and the zoom keys scale the distance; place_camera then positions the camera and points it at the stack. Launching uses the camera's ray, so it aims correctly from any angle.
  • Drawing. Each body has an ordinary MeshInstance3D. After every step, sync_nodes copies each body's pose onto its node. The nodes never feed back into the simulation.
  • Cleanup. box_tower_exit_tree destroys the world when the scene closes.

Densities are in kg/m³, and Box3D's default is 1000 (water). The boxes use 250 and the ball 4000, so each box weighs about 128 kg and the ball about 450 kg. Set densities explicitly: with the default, a small ball barely moves a large box.

Going further#

  • Add interpolation if you render faster than 60 Hz: the nodes currently move only on physics frames.
  • For editor-authored worlds, saved checkpoints, rollback or multiplayer, use the Kit and Replay samples. The raw API is described in box3d/README.md.
